title: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI)
note: Official PSI portal (site root). Investigation-level datasets are linked individually on each investigation record.

title: PSI Data Repository: Combustion Science
note: Challenge resource 01. The repository search returns 26 investigations for 'combustion'; 24 have Research Area 'Combustion Science' and were ingested through the public PSI JSON endpoints (metadata, DOIs, publications, experiment tables).

title: Combustion Science
note: Challenge resource 02. Program overview: why microgravity removes buoyancy, ISS combustion facilities (CIR, MDCA). Article text extracted and indexed.

title: NASA ScienceCasts: The Power of Studying Combustion on the ISS
note: Challenge resource 03. Published 2018-03-13; duration 219 s. Video metadata only — no transcript was extracted, so the video content is not searchable and is never used as evidence.

title: A Researcher's Guide to: Combustion Science (October 2015)
note: Challenge resource 04. Authors: Gokoglu, Dietrich, Stocker, Ferkul, Olson, Hicks. Report NP-2015-10-034-JSC. Full text extracted page by page (55 of 56 pages contain text; page 4 is image-only) and indexed with page references.

title: Apollo 1 (AS-204)
publisher: NASA Office of Safety and Mission Assurance
note: Challenge resource 05. Historical spacecraft fire (1967 pad test). Mission history — not a combustion experiment.

title: Apollo 13
publisher: NASA Office of Safety and Mission Assurance
note: Challenge resource 06. Oxygen-tank explosion (1970). Mission history — not a combustion experiment.

title: 25 Years Ago: Fire Aboard Space Station Mir
note: Challenge resource 07. Article by John Uri, 2022-02-23, on the 1997 oxygen-generator fire. Mission history — not a combustion experiment.

title: Fireman's Air Tanks
note: Challenge resource 08. Spacesuit-derived lightweight firefighter breathing tanks. Technology transfer — not experimental evidence.

title: Fire Detector
note: Challenge resource 09. Shuttle-era incipient fire detector that discriminates combustion particles from dust. Technology transfer — not experimental evidence.

title: New Technology for the Fire Attire
note: Challenge resource 10. Project FIRES: spacesuit/spacecraft thermal-protection materials applied to firefighter gear. Technology transfer — not experimental evidence.
